picks.style: ancient greek tragic lament, plaintive aulos and low lyre with drone, solo female voice, slow, keening, darkening
picks.why: The farewell to the children — 'the sweet embrace, the soft young cheek, the fragrant breath' — is the play's heart and needs no context.

picks.style: ancient chorus, kithara and frame drum, layered female voices in unison, incantatory, striding, defiant
picks.why: 'Back to their source the holy rivers turn their tide' — a world-reversal ode that opens with the line everyone remembers.

picks.style: greek choral threnody, lyre and reed pipe, massed voices, mournful, hymn-like, unhurried
picks.why: 'O my country, O my own dear home!' — a clean exile lament with a natural refrain shape.

picks.style: ancient greek chorus, phrygian reed pipes and lyre, layered female voices, pastoral opening turning ominous, moderate sway
picks.why: Paris piping among the white heifers of Ida — a pastoral image that turns into the cause of a war, all in one breath.

picks.style: greek tragic monody, solo young female voice, sparse aulos and soft kithara, free rhythm, plaintive, fading
picks.why: Iphigenia's monody: the snow-beat glen, the fountains of the Nymphs, hyacinths and rose-buds — grief rendered entirely as landscape.

picks.style: processional greek narrative chant, low lyre and frame drum, declamatory male voice with choral answers, solemn, steadily building
picks.why: The messenger's account of the girl offering her own neck — the single most famous moment in the play.

picks.style: baroque martial ode, natural trumpets and full strings, commanding tenor, stately, grand, processional
picks.why: Contains Addison's most quoted lines — the angel who 'Rides in the Whirl-wind, and directs the Storm'.

picks.style: english baroque ode, harpsichord and viol consort, clear countertenor, surging, awestruck, quickening
picks.why: A deluge in tetrameter quatrains — 'All Nature's floating Ruins ride' — already shaped like a hymn stanza.

picks.style: sacred oratorio chorus, organ and trumpets, massed voices, majestic, thunderous, slow build
picks.why: The last trump and the graves conceiving; 'kindred Atoms rally into Men' is a startling image for 1700.

picks.style: english pastoral art song, flute and harpsichord, clear soprano, nocturnal, unhurried, moonlit
picks.why: A proper invocation — 'All hail! majestic Queen of Night' — opening a nocturne that stands alone.

picks.style: 18th century fairy dance-song, pizzicato strings and tambourine, light bright voices, quick, tripping, mischievous
picks.why: Fairies 'beating the pansie-paven ground in frolic measures round and round' — the rhythm is already a dance.

picks.style: georgian pastoral ballad, acoustic guitar and fiddle, plain tenor, lilting triple time, wistful
picks.why: Complete ballad stanzas ending on a clean farewell to the maiden — singable as written.

picks.style: georgian ode of encouragement, chamber strings and harpsichord, bright soprano, rising, stately, hopeful
picks.why: 'Be ever rising, rise thou ne'er so high' — the argument for a woman's learning at its most direct and lifted.

picks.style: italianate 18th century canzonetta, harpsichord and pizzicato strings, dry wry tenor, brisk, light-footed
picks.why: The veteran showing his scars and the freed galley-slave showing his shackles — a witty song with a real sting.

picks.style: english baroque love song, lute and viola da gamba, plaintive countertenor, slow, cool, aching
picks.why: Warm Italian valleys, then pale sunbeams on everlasting snow — one clean simile for a woman's coldness.

picks.style: english pastoral art song, cello and guitar, warm baritone, unhurried, contemplative, evening
picks.why: The pensioned sailor safe ashore, meditating on 'his great voyage, to the world unknown' — a quiet, complete ending.

picks.style: 18th century drinking song, boisterous strings and hand drum, rowdy male voice with chorus, fast, swaggering, refrain-driven
picks.why: 'Haste away, haste away, lash thy tigers do not stay' — a built-in refrain and a genuine bacchic pulse.

picks.style: georgian pastoral song, flute and harpsichord, sweet soprano, flowing, tender
picks.why: A whole small song: the paradise catalogued, then dismissed the moment she appears.

picks.style: victorian parlour hymn, upright piano and fiddle, plain earnest male voice, steady march, resolute
picks.why: Only candidate available; 'the virtue lies in the struggle, not the prize' and Burns's 'glorious privilege of being independent' carry it.
